purpose: Prove the proposed P4 Docker Compose configuration before starting containers.

findings.evidence: A first dry run using only --env-file still loaded the repo-root .env through docker-compose.yml service env_file entries. That would inject old source .env values into the P4 containers.
A temporary Compose override using env_file: !reset [] for openclaw-gateway and openclaw-cli removed repo-root .env injection from the rendered service environments.
Rendered openclaw-gateway ports publish target 18789 to host_ip 127.0.0.1 published 18789 and target 18790 to host_ip 127.0.0.1 published 18790.

A follow-up JSON parse of rendered Compose output produced exact tuples [('127.0.0.1', '18789', 18789), ('127.0.0.1', '18790', 18790)], proving both ports rather than only grepping for one loopback host_ip occurrence.
Rendered volumes bind /opt/openclaw-data/runtime/openclaw-foundation-sandbox/config, workspace, and auth-profile-secrets to the expected container paths.
Rendered service environments after override did not include the old /opt/openclaw-data/workspace/openclaw-foundation-sandbox/runtime paths that appeared in the failed dry run.
Rendered services retain cap_drop NET_RAW and NET_ADMIN plus no-new-privileges:true.

required_packet_change: The P4 apply command must write and use a Compose override that resets service env_file entries before pull, config set, or up.
not_performed: No Docker image was pulled or built.
No container was created or started.
